question: Can a process-local, user-space mechanism observe and enforce the compiled reader ACTUAL OS file operations without elevated privilege?
answer: NO on this host. Two independent mechanisms attempted; both fail. Blocker preserved.

mechanisms_attempted.name: DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES + plain symbol definitions
mechanisms_attempted.failure: plain function definitions do NOT interpose libsystem symbols that live in the dyld shared cache
mechanisms_attempted.diagnosis: because even a DIRECT ctypes libc.open() produced zero events, this is a mechanism defect, not a pyreadstat bypass

mechanisms_attempted.name: DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES + __DATA,__interpose tuples
mechanisms_attempted.diagnosis: interposing open or stat or even a cold symbol (getpid) breaks interpreter startup on BOTH available interpreters

alternative_mechanisms_considered.name: FSEvents
alternative_mechanisms_considered.reason: directory-change notifications, not per-open accounting; would also require opening a source directory, which is forbidden

limits_of_the_attempted_method_even_if_i: would observe libc symbol entries in the calling process, NOT kernel audit records
could not see operations issued as raw syscalls bypassing interposed libc symbols
would be a measurement basis distinct from a kernel open(2) count and would be labelled as such
